prose_updates.tldr: For fixed donor count, pre grid, post grid, and exact rank of the fixed donor-pre matrix, the required positive rank-\(r\) separation follows from \(\sigma_r(M)>0=\sigma_{r+1}(M)\); no additional singular-gap assumption is imposed. Covariate-adjusted cross-fitted AIPCW cell estimates have a joint root-\(K\) expansion conditional on explicit bounded-variation and relative-variation restrictions for the selected event learner. A clipped empirical hazard learner satisfies those restrictions with \(a_K=K^{-1/2}\) on a fixed finite-stratum submodel, but this certificate is not a generic learner result and does not verify the TCL application. Exact post-transport, without a global target-pre row-space assumption, identifies the untreated potential curve with the observed-law spectral representation. The full three-block spectral derivative yields a possibly singular joint Gaussian law; positive coordinate variances suffice for the simultaneous band and a positive grid-RMST variance suffices for scalar studentization. A full-data causal construction, preserving all six observed margins, proves that unadjusted Kaplan--Meier/PCR has fixed bias on a relatively open subclass. Weak-gap and selected-rank inference remains open.

project_justification.niche: With \(N_0,T_0,J,r\) fixed and \(K\to\infty\), covariate-standardized cell curves form a finite-dimensional semiparametric first stage. Exact rank of the fixed donor-pre matrix itself gives \(\sigma_r(M)>0=\sigma_{r+1}(M)\), so the counterfactual is a smooth local spectral functional without a separate singular-gap assumption. The bridge requires the exact Stieltjes remainder under a disclosed learner-path variation restriction, a concrete submodel on which that restriction is attainable, and all three terms of the pseudoinverse derivative.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The positive theory is fixed-dimensional and conditional on an event learner whose relative-survival path has the stated bounded variation and \(L_2\) variation rate. Ordinary supremum or \(L_2\) consistency does not imply that property. The finite-stratum hazard certificate establishes attainability only for fixed covariate and event-time supports with uniformly positive at-risk probabilities, event hazards bounded away from one, and proportional training samples; it does not verify the restriction for generic learners or for the TCL data. For the fixed matrix \(M\), exact rank already supplies the positive local rank-\(r\) separation used in differentiation, so there is no standalone singular-gap restriction. This argument is not uniform over triangular arrays with \(\sigma_r(M_K)\to0\). The joint Gaussian covariance may be singular, but the band excludes zero counterfactual coordinate variances and the grid-RMST interval excludes zero variance in its scalar direction. The theory does not cover growing grids or panels, selected rank, approximate post-transport, or continuous-time RMST.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The joint cell expansion is a conditional-learner theorem under within-cell i.i.d. sampling, cross-cell independence for stacking, conditional independent censoring, censor positivity, fixed-fold nuisance consistency and product rate, origin normalization, and explicit bounded-variation and relative-variation restrictions. A concrete clipped empirical hazard learner discharges the event-side restrictions with root-\(K\) rate only on the stated fixed finite-stratum submodel; this does not establish generic learner attainability or verify the 925-patient TCL application. The spectral limit additionally requires fixed panel dimensions, exact rank of the fixed donor-pre matrix, and exact post-transport, which is its sole global causal-identification equality. Exact rank implies the fixed positive separation \(\sigma_r(M)>0=\sigma_{r+1}(M)\), so no separate singular-gap assumption is required; the result is not uniform for a sequence of matrices with a closing gap. No global target-pre row-space assumption is imposed: the Han--Shah embedding derives row membership from its own factor-span hypotheses, and the full-data rational witness derives it from invertibility. The witness explicitly separates treated and untreated target-post potential times, imposes consistency, preserves all six observed margins, and proves a relatively open causal subclass with fixed Kaplan--Meier/PCR bias. The joint covariance may be singular. The simultaneous band requires positive counterfactual marginal variances, and the studentized grid-RMST interval separately requires positive variance of \(q^\top(\Phi_1-\Phi_\theta)\). Applying either conclusion to TCL requires independent verification of all sampling, learner, transport, and relevant variance conditions. Nothing here covers growing dimensions, selected rank, approximate transport, or continuous-time RMST. Weak-gap inference remains the acknowledged follow-on question because its frontier also depends on weak loadings and a uniform triangular experiment, not only on \(\sigma_r(M_K)\).

statement_notes.justification: The theorem supplies a full three-block root-\(K\) law with consistently estimated covariance, permits a singular Gaussian limit, uses exact post-transport rather than target-pre row membership for causal identification, and derives local spectral separation from fixed-matrix exact rank rather than imposing a redundant singular-gap assumption.
statement_notes.gap: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) analyze marginal cellwise Kaplan--Meier/PCR inputs; Westling et al. (2024, published Theorem 3 (arXiv Theorem 4)) analyze a directly estimated covariate-adjusted survival curve. Neither gives the full three-block influence vector or its possibly singular joint covariance law.
statement_notes.consumer: The theorem could provide TCL standard errors only if its within-cell sampling, cross-cell independence, learner, fixed-matrix exact-rank, exact post-transport, and application-specific variance conditions are verified; no separate singular-gap condition is needed in this fixed-matrix regime.
